title: Identities vs equations
examples: When do we use the triple bar symbol?
How do I use comparing coefficients?

explain.say: Today we look at identities versus equations. An equation has an equals sign. An identity uses a triple bar symbol.
An equation is only true for certain values. An identity is true for all values you put in. Think of it as always being balanced.
We can test if something is an identity. We substitute a number for the variable. If it works every time, it is an identity.

items: Substitute a number for the variable
If it works every time, it is an identity

explain.say: Comparing coefficients is a strong method. If two polynomials are identical, their coefficients must match. This helps find unknown constants.
For example, if x squared plus a x plus five is an identity, then a must equal zero. We compare the x times x parts.

faq.q: What is the difference between an equation and an identity?
faq.a: An equation only works for some specific numbers. An identity is always true no matter what number you use.

faq.q: Why do we use the triple bar symbol?
faq.a: The triple bar symbol means the statement is an identity. It shows it is true for all values of the variable.

faq.q: How do I use comparing coefficients?
faq.a: You set the two sides equal and then match the coefficients of each power of the variable. This gives you equations to solve.
asks: Can I use this method for everything?

faq.q: If I test it with one number, does that prove it's an identity?
faq.a: No, testing with one number is not enough proof. You must test more numbers or use comparing coefficients.
asks: What if it works for two numbers?

faq.q: Can I compare coefficients if there are no variables?
faq.a: Yes, you can compare the constant terms. These are the numbers without any variable attached to them.
asks: Do I compare the numbers only?

facts: An equation uses the equals sign, =

quiz.say: If x squared plus two x plus one is an identity, what is the value of the constant term?
quiz.why: The constant term is the number without x, and in this case, it is one.

wrong.0: This option includes the variable x, so it is not a constant.
wrong.1: This is a variable term, not the constant part of the expression.
wrong.3: This is the coefficient of the x term, not the constant term.

quiz.say: Which statement correctly uses the symbol for an identity?
quiz.why: The triple bar symbol means the statement is true for all values of a and b.

wrong.0: The question mark suggests it needs to be checked, not that it is always true.
wrong.2: The equals sign suggests it might only be true for some values.
wrong.3: The not equal sign suggests it is never true, which is incorrect.

quiz.say: If the identity is 3x squared plus k x plus 7, and it must equal 3x squared plus 5x plus 7, what is k?
quiz.why: We compare the coefficients of the x term; k must equal 5 for the identity to hold.

wrong.0: We are solving for the value of k, not writing the variable itself.
wrong.2: This is the coefficient of the x squared term, not the x term.
wrong.3: This is the constant term, which we are not comparing here.
